summary.text: A bathyscaphe is a self-propelled deep-sea submersible whose crew cabin hangs beneath a float instead of from a cable to the surface.
Its float holds gasoline, which barely compresses, so the tanks can be lightly built while the crew cabin must be massive to resist the pressure.
To rise it drops iron shot held by an electromagnet, so if the power fails the shot falls out and the craft ascends on its own.

facts.label: First bathyscaphe
facts.value: FNRS-2, built in Belgium from 1946 to 1948

facts.label: Deepest dive
facts.value: Trieste reached the Challenger Deep in 1960

items.prompt: A designer needs something lighter than water to fill a bathyscaphe's float for very deep dives. Why pick a liquid like gasoline over a gas?

options.label: It also fuels the motors that drive the craft
It barely compresses, so the tanks need no strong walls
It keeps the crew cabin warm in cold water
It is heavier than seawater, which aids the descent

items.explain: Gasoline is buoyant in water yet practically incompressible, so pressure inside and outside the tanks evens out and they can be lightly built.

items.prompt: A submarine surfaces by blowing compressed air into its flooded tanks. Why can't a bathyscaphe do this at the depths it was built for?

options.label: Its hull is too thin to hold compressed air
Compressed air would freeze in the cold deep water
The water pressure there is too great to push out
It carries no air supply because the cabin is sealed

items.explain: At those depths the water pressure is too great; at the bottom of the Challenger Deep it is more than seven times the pressure in a standard compressed gas cylinder.

items.prompt: Deep on a dive, a bathyscaphe suddenly loses all electrical power. What happens next?

options.label: Iron shot pours out and the craft rises by itself
It stays at that depth until power is restored
It sinks further as its float tanks fill with water
The crew must pump out the tanks by hand

items.explain: The shot is held in open-bottomed hoppers by an electromagnet; without power it runs out by gravity, so ascent is automatic and needs no power.

items.prompt: On a bathyscaphe, why are the float tanks thin-walled while the crew cabin is extremely heavy?

options.label: The cabin must carry the weight of the iron shot
The float is replaced after every dive, so it is cheap
The cabin is built heavy to help the craft sink
Only the cabin faces a big pressure difference

items.explain: Pressure inside and outside the gasoline tanks equalizes, but the crew cabin must withstand a huge pressure differential, so it is massively built.

items.prompt: At the surface, the crew want the bathyscaphe to float a little lower before a dive. What do they put into the float tanks?

options.label: Extra gasoline pumped in from the support ship
Compressed air to fill the empty space
Water in place of some of the gasoline
More iron shot packed into the float

items.explain: Water is denser than gasoline, so swapping some gasoline for water easily trims the craft's buoyancy at the surface.

items.prompt: In 1960 the Trieste crew shone a light on the floor of the Challenger Deep and reported a flatfish about a foot long. Which open question did they say this settled?

options.label: Whether animals can live that deep in total darkness
Whether the seafloor there was made of solid rock
Whether sound can travel to the deepest seafloor
Whether a lamp can work under such high pressure

items.explain: Seeing a fish lying on the seabed put to rest the question of whether there was life at such a depth in the complete absence of light.
